reason: The target is a commencement provision and has no ongoing operative study content.
The definitions section supplies core estate-administration terms for the Act.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Definitions for Devolution of Estates Act concepts
proposedGroups.reason: The target defines family, court, property, chattel, and representative concepts while one former term is repealed.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Identify the defined concepts used in the Devolution of Estates Act.

reason: The target states the temporal scope of Part I by date of death.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Application of Part I by date of death

focusSelections.evidenceText: applies only in cases of death occurring after its commencement

proposedGroups.reason: The rule is limited to when Part I applies.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Determine whether Part I applies based on the date of death.

reason: The section vests real and personal property in personal representatives as trustees on death.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Devolution of property to personal representatives
proposedGroups.reason: The rule covers property subject to debts and dispositions and general powers of appointment exercised by will.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Explain how real and personal property devolves to personal representatives on death.

reason: The section extends personal-property probate and administration rules to real property vested in representatives.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Probate and administration jurisdiction applied to real property

focusSelections.evidenceText: applies to real property vesting in these representatives

proposedGroups.reason: The rule also limits sale or transfer by fewer than all joint representatives without Court authority.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recognize how probate and administration law applies to real property in a personal representative.

reason: The section preserves specified rights and interests despite appointment of a personal representative.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Preserved rights despite personal representative appointment

focusSelections.evidenceText: does not, save as hereinafter provided, affect

proposedGroups.reason: The preserved matters include marshalling, beneficial interests, dealings with those interests, and recovery proceedings.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Identify rights and interests not displaced by appointing a personal representative.

reason: The target requires real property to be administered like personal property for estate liabilities while preserving beneficiary asset-order rules.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Administration of real property as personal property

focusSelections.evidenceText: real property shall be administered in the same manner

proposedGroups.reason: The rule covers debts, costs, expenses, incidents, and preserved order between beneficiaries.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Apply the rule treating real property as personal property in estate administration.

reason: The section deems the personal representative the heir for interpretation while real property remains vested in the representative.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Personal representative deemed heir for vested real property

focusSelections.evidenceText: shall, while the estate remains in him, be deemed in law the heir

proposedGroups.reason: The deeming rule applies unless a contrary intention appears and does not affect beneficial rights.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recognize when a personal representative is deemed the heir.

reason: The section provides separate post-one-year remedies for compelled conveyance and court-ordered sale.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Court-ordered conveyance to person entitled to real property
proposedGroups.reason: This subsection allows an entitled person to seek conveyance or vesting after request and personal representative failure.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Identify when the Court may order conveyance or vesting to the person entitled.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Court-ordered sale when personal representative has not conveyed or sold
proposedGroups.reason: This subsection allows a beneficially interested person to seek sale and possible sheriff sale after non-compliance.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Determine when the Court may order sale after personal representative inaction.

reason: The target authorizes sale of real property for debts and distribution and states when concurrence matters.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Personal representative sale power for debts or distribution

focusSelections.evidenceText: not only of paying debts but also of distributing the estate

proposedGroups.reason: The sale may occur whether or not there are debts, with concurrence needed for distribution-only sales.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Identify the purposes for sale and when beneficiary concurrence matters.

reason: The section distinguishes the concurrence requirement from court approval where concurrence is unavailable or incomplete.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Concurrence requirement for distribution-only real property sales
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections require concurrence and deem it when an adult knowingly accepts purchase money.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recognize when a beneficiary is treated as concurring in a distribution-only sale.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Court approval where beneficiaries cannot or do not concur
proposedGroups.reason: This subsection permits court approval binding persons lacking capacity, non-concurring adults, contingent interests, and unascertained beneficiaries.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Apply the court approval route when concurrence is missing or impossible.

reason: The section makes sales involving a minor invalid without guardian consent or Court order.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Sale of real property where a minor is interested
proposedGroups.reason: The rule requires written guardian consent or approval, or absent that, an order of the Court.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Identify the consent or court order needed for a sale involving a minor.

reason: The target allows division, partition, and conveyance with adult concurrence and required approvals for minors or represented persons.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Division or conveyance of real property among beneficiaries

focusSelections.evidenceText: divide or partition and convey the real property

proposedGroups.reason: The rule names concurrence and approval conditions for interested persons.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Determine the approvals needed before division or conveyance among beneficiaries.

reason: The section authorizes leasing and mortgaging estate real property and identifies where Court approval is required.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Leasing and mortgaging estate real property

focusSelections.evidenceText: lease the real property or any part thereof

proposedGroups.reason: The listed powers include short leases, longer court-approved leases, and mortgages for debts, taxes, improvements, or estate benefit.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Identify the powers to lease or mortgage estate real property and when Court approval is required.

reason: Purchaser protection and continuing liability after conveyance to beneficiaries are separate rules.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Good-faith purchaser protection from estate debts and beneficiary claims
proposedGroups.reason: This subsection protects good-faith value purchasers except for specific non-will charges and beneficiary claims in some sales.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recognize the protection given to good-faith purchasers of estate real property.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Continuing liability of property conveyed to beneficiaries
proposedGroups.reason: This subsection keeps conveyed or vested property liable for deceased-owner debts and creates limited personal liability after value transactions.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Determine how estate debts continue to affect property conveyed or vested in beneficiaries.

reason: The target requires concurrence of all personal representatives or a Court order, with a proving-executor exception.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Concurrence of multiple personal representatives

focusSelections.evidenceText: without the concurrence therein of all such representatives

proposedGroups.reason: The exception applies where probate is granted to one or some named executors.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Identify when all personal representatives must concur and the proving-executor exception.

reason: The section separates the court order for sale free from curtesy or dower from the sale effect and compensation options.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Court order for sale free from curtesy or dower
proposedGroups.reason: This subsection allows a personal representative to apply for a summary order with notice unless otherwise directed.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Identify when a personal representative may seek sale free from curtesy or dower.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Effect of sale and compensation for curtesy or dower interests
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections pass the interest without release and authorize gross-sum, annual-sum, income, and investment orders.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Explain the effect of sale and compensation for curtesy or dower interests.

reason: The section states that Act rights and immunities supplement other statutory or will powers.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Act rights and immunities are additional

focusSelections.evidenceText: in addition to and not in derogation

proposedGroups.reason: The rule prevents reading the Act as reducing other powers of personal representatives.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recognize that the Act adds to rather than displaces other powers.
